reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its primary purpose is practical instruction on checking Windows compatibility and creating Windows 10 installation media with a USB drive. The frames show Windows system requirements, a Microsoft download page, and setup selections for language, edition, and architecture. The subscribe prompt and Dell social links indicate ordinary channel engagement and support contact information, without a financial offer, payment request, credential request, or deceptive transaction.

citations.quote: How to Create Windows 10 Installation Media (Official Dell Tech Support)
In this video we'll show you how to create windows installation media using a USB Flash Drive.
Before starting the process there are a few things to verify pertaining to compatibility for the PC on which Windows 10 will be installed.

opening.argument: The video links acquisition of a digital installation asset to a concrete viewer action: users are directed to Microsoft, told to select “download tool now,” and then create installation media on a USB drive. The description supplies multiple external download and support links, while the instructions require a blank drive and warn that its contents will be deleted. That is a low-friction acquisition funnel presented as routine support, with the practical consequence tied directly to clicking, downloading, and preparing removable media. The material does not establish that the resulting media is safe, genuine, or suitable for the viewer’s specific device; it mainly directs the viewer through the acquisition process.

citations.quote: Go to microsoft.com and search for Download Windows 10, this link is also provided in the description. Select download tool now and then run.
Last but not least, get yourself a blank USB flash drive with at least eight gigs of space and insert it into the PC you will be using for the download of the tool.
Be sure to use a blank drive because anything saved on it will be deleted.
MS Windows Installation Media Tool Download https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/software-download/windows10

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account calls this practical instruction, but its own cited excerpts confirm that viewers are being directed to download software and prepare a removable drive. A title calling the source “Official Dell Tech Support” does not prove that the download path is safe for every viewer. Nor do compatibility checks eliminate the central concern: the instructions still push viewers toward an external download and irreversible deletion of existing USB contents.

citations.quote: How to Create Windows 10 Installation Media (Official Dell Tech Support)
Be sure to use a blank drive because anything saved on it will be deleted.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited instructions show acquisition of installation media, not a promised reward, payment, withdrawal, or other benefit. “Download tool now” is an ordinary software-download instruction, and the warning that USB contents will be deleted is an explicit risk disclosure rather than concealment. The material also says the video focuses on media creation, so these quotes do not establish a deceptive acquisition offer.

citations.quote: Please note that this video content focuses on media creation only.
Be sure to use a blank drive because anything saved on it will be deleted.

opening.argument: Several genuine risk signals appear together: the viewer must use an external download, run a tool as an administrator, choose system-specific settings, and surrender all existing USB contents. The description also presents a long collection of external Microsoft, Dell, social-media, and community links. That combination makes the process unusually dependent on links and privileged access while placing the burden of compatibility and data loss on the viewer. The tutorial’s calm technical framing can make those risks seem routine, even though the supplied material does not independently establish who controls every linked destination or what happens if the selected edition, architecture, or language is wrong.

citations.quote: To be able to run the tool you will need to be an administrator for your PC.
Now select the desired language, the Windows 10 edition, the proper architecture, and the media you want to use
Now using the link in the description, visit the Microsoft specification and system's requirements page to be sure your PC meets the minimum requirements.
If you have questions or need support, contact us through social media on Facebook at www.facebook.com/dell and Twitter at www.twitter.com/dellcares

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account emphasizes visible requirements pages and setup selections, but those details do not remove the risk signals. Compatibility advice still requires viewers to follow an external link, and the setup still requires administrator access and an edition, architecture, and language choice. The cited frames show screens, not independent proof that every link, download, or resulting installation is appropriate for the individual viewer.

citations.quote: To be able to run the tool you will need to be an administrator for your PC.
Now select the desired language, the Windows 10 edition, the proper architecture, and the media you want to use

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are disclosed operational prerequisites, not evidence of a scam. The video expressly tells viewers to check system requirements, identifies the Microsoft download location, and warns that the USB contents will be deleted. Nothing cited shows a payment request, credential collection, concealed charge, or promised return; administrator access is needed to run the tool, not presented as a benefit claim.

opening.argument: Although presented as support, the video functions as a branded promotion for a linked ecosystem and its digital downloads. It identifies itself as “Official Dell Tech Support,” directs viewers to Microsoft’s Windows download flow, supplies Dell social and community channels, and ends by asking viewers to subscribe. The operational lesson therefore doubles as a participation pathway: viewers are moved from branded authority to an external download, then back toward Dell-controlled engagement. That promotional structure is relevant because the digital installation media is acquired only after following the directed actions, while the material does not establish that the viewer receives any independent benefit beyond the promoted workflow.

citations.quote: How to Create Windows 10 Installation Media (Official Dell Tech Support)
Go to microsoft.com and search for Download Windows 10, this link is also provided in the description.
Anytime you need help or have questions, you can contact us on Facebook or Twitter.
If you liked this video give it a like and thanks for watching.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material a tutorial does not answer the promotional structure. The title foregrounds Dell authority, the instructions send viewers to Microsoft, and the closing directs viewers to Dell’s social channels and engagement prompts. Those are not necessary to explain every technical step; they steer viewers through a branded network while the promised practical outcome depends on following the download process.

citations.quote: How to Create Windows 10 Installation Media (Official Dell Tech Support)
Anytime you need help or have questions, you can contact us on Facebook or Twitter.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Branding and ordinary channel engagement do not convert technical education into a scam. The cited title accurately describes the subject, and the instructions identify the Microsoft source rather than hiding it. The closing engagement language does not promise money, assets, or special access. Most importantly, the material describes installation media creation, not a deceptive reward or acquisition scheme.
